title: Twin Dial
description: A twin round-dial instrument cluster for the G20 panel: tachometer left, speedometer right, our own centre pages and check-control message

de.bmw.body.Light._about: the tab key (config.tabKey): the stalk's TRIP button, bit 0x40 of operationColumnStalks; notifier 32773 only (no getter), so s. Verified on the car 2026-11-18. Read only.

de.bmw.infotainment.vehicle.Vehicle2._about: statusDisplayedCCMessage (getter 61): the number of the message the cluster displays, the second witness beside KombiIF.statusActiveCCMessage (SPEC 8.4). Read only; unseen on the car until probe P1.

de.bmw.infrastructure.VehicleInformation._about: Range (notifier 32770, no getter): the odometer's third carrier (research3/MK, config.odometer.order)

de.bmw.infrastructure.MileageSupreme._about: getter 1 / notifier 32769: the odometer's second carrier, with its qualifier (research3/MK, config.odometer.order). Read only.

de.bmw.infrastructure.SecureMileage._about: getter 1 / notifier 32769: the odometer's fourth carrier (research3/MK, config.odometer.order). Read only; manipulationState is logged as a number, never used.

de.bmw.infotainment.resetlogic.ResetLogi._about: getter 7 / notifier 32775: the head unit's own trip computer, the fallback for every trip value behind KombiIF (research3/MK, config.trip.order). Read only.

de.bmw.infotainment.drivingexcitement.FE._about: statusSwitchDriveDynamicSport2 (getter 39 / notifier 32807): displayBoostPressure, the technical page's boost row (round 3 B4; the engine already reads it: hud.js boostFes). Read only.

de.bmw.infrastructure.EnvironmentalInfor._about: UnitBN2020.unitOfMeasurementMileage (getter 1): unseen (P5); round 2 only logs it and keeps km

de.bmw.infotainment.KombiIF._about: statusRangeTankStatus: fuel litres, range km, spare (reserve) and mileageKilometre (the odometer, first carrier). The trip computer fields are unseen (P4); research3/MK: the most likely factors are on by default (config.trip), each value UNVERIFIED in the log until the first drive compares it with the car's trip page. statusActiveCCMessage / statusMenuCCMessage: READ ONLY (standardCCMessage / extendedCCMessage are setters and are never declared).

de.bmw.infotainment.KombiInterface_2._about: ccList only (live on the car); newCCMessage never arrived and requestDefaultSymbols is not used: our own symbols (SPEC 8.3)

de.bmw.infotainment.hmi.hmimediastate.Hm._about: unseen (P8): playerMetadata, trackProgress, menu feed the tab-3 pages (config.pages.media, dark); the text is drawn, never logged (lengths only). coverArt is NOT declared (up to 850 kB a notification).

de.bmw.infotainment.connectivity.telepho._about: unseen (P9): an enum only, no number or name is read

de.bmw.infotainment.navigation.navigatio._about: the navigation tab's icon: lit while a route is guided

de.bmw.infotainment.tuner.fmamdab.tunerf._about: unseen (P8): the radio page (config.pages.media, dark). Read only.

de.bmw.infotainment.entertainment.mediap._about: unseen (P8): CarPlay track n of m and play state, one instance per interface (SPEC-R3 4.3). Read only.

de.bmw.infotainment.connectivity.telepho.name: rs
de.bmw.infotainment.connectivity.telepho._about: unseen (P9): the call card (config.pages.phone, dark). name is private: kept only while the setting "callerName" is on and the call lasts, never logged. Read only.
unseen (P9): the muted-microphone mark on the call card. Read only (its setter is never declared).

de.bmw.infotainment.devicemanager.device._about: unseen (P9): the idle phone page (connected, path, battery, signal); friendlyName and persistentAttributes are never read. Read only.

de.bmw.infotainment.navigation.guiding.G._about: unseen (P12): the road line, the guidance page (config.pages.guidance, dark) and the map window's presence rule (config.mapWindow). Road text is drawn, never logged; positions and bearings are never read. Read only.

de.bmw.infotainment.vehicle.TPMS._about: the tyre page (config.pages.tyres, dark): the car never notifies TPMS, so the page reads the getters every 10 s while it shows (shared/twin_pages.js tpmsPoll). Read only.

de.bmw.dass.driverassistanceapplications._about: SPEC-R3 8 and 9 (package B5). Both notifier only (32769 / 32772, no getter), flag s: nothing here is a getter, a setter or a method. displaySpeedLimitAndNoPassingRestriction: the sign (config.sign, copied from f30_cluster as it is). displayDriverAssistanceLongitudinal: the cruise / limiter's struct, UNSEEN on the car until the car session (SPEC 9); read and logged (numbers and enum names), drawn only while config.cruise is set. That the sign field arrives is not yet shown by a log line in the repository: the build logs 'limit:' lines (shared/twin_limit.js) and the car session confirms.

config._comment: target panel: the whole 1920x720 instrument cluster (docs/twin-dial/SPEC.md 14). tankLitres: the fuel bar's full mark (the car sends litres, not the tank size; the owner confirms 59). carGroups: the signal groups hud.js asks the kit's Car for (no accel / torque: twin_dial declares neither). redline: the setting 'redline' wins. trip.factors / odometer.factors: on by default since research3/MK, corrected here (never in code) after the first drive (docs/research3/MK-PROTOCOL.md).
config._legacyProbes: package F: f30_cluster's 0.7.18 log probes (ccListRiskClass, basicList, requestDefaultSymbols) must not run in twin_dial; hud.js _legacyProbesOff() reads this. config.probe is NOT here: the probe build adds it (apps/twin_dial/probe/probe.json, package F)

twin._about: shared/twin_tokens.js (the {{td:...}} tokens and the centre pages' cycle): switches the app's extra signal wiring on

tabs._about: SPEC-R3 3: live tabs on (shared/twin_tabs.js, package B2; the key absent = live tabs off, the round 2 look). lockAboveKmh: used while the app has no tabLock setting. messageTab false: a message does not select tab 2. callSelects: rule 2, a call rings or runs -> tab 4; OFF until the car session has shown the call state (probe P9)

tabKey._verified: THE CAR, 2026-11-18 (signal_probe log, the owner confirmed the presses): the stalk's TRIP button is bit 0x40 of de.bmw.body.Light IndicatorSteeringColumn.operationColumnStalks (UInt8, notifier 32773, no getter: declared s). 17 presses gave 17 clean 0 -> 0x40 -> 0 pairs, held about 0.15 s, about 0.5 s apart. The rising edge only is a press (shared/twin_tabs.js keyHandler); 255 is the catalogue's unfilled default (every bit set) and counts as no state.

config._tabKey: SPEC-R3 R9: the tab key source, null until the car session (docs/AGENT-BRIEF-car-signals.md, probe P13) finds a field that moves on one press. Forms: {"iface": "...", "field": "...", "path": ["member"], "mask": 64} (a bit), {..., "press": [1, "TASTER_GEDRUECKT"]} (a level; the rising edge counts), {..., "counter": true} (a step counter), {..., "any": true} (any change); optional "instance", "dir" (1 | -1), "rateMs". The field must also be in "signals" (rs / s): the key reads, it never writes. shared/twin_tabs.js

factors._verified: THE CAR, 2026-11-18, against the car's own trip page (15.5 l/100 km, 13.7 km/h, 19.2 km, 1:28): KombiIF speed x 0.1, consumption x 0.1, distance x 1 (NOT 0.1), board computer 1; hours and minutes plain. rl3 (ResetLogic3) is still unverified.

trip._about: research3/MK (the owner, 2026-11-18: no dashes by design). factors: the unit of each raw integer (km/h, l/100 km, km per bit; bc 1 or 2 = which KombiIF board computer), the most likely ones ON by default; a key left out takes the same default, false switches the page back to dashes. rl3: the same for ResetLogic3.bcDataAll (speedAverage, consumptionCombustionAverageDigit, counterDistance). order: per value, the first source with a valid value wins (kombi = KombiIF statusBordcomputerAverage / TravelData / TravelStart, rl3 = ResetLogic3). departureUtc: the sources whose departure time is UTC (e.g. ['rl3']) are moved into the car's zone. verified: false = the first arrival of each source is logged UNVERIFIED (compare with the car's own trip page, docs/research3/MK-PROTOCOL.md); set true once it matches. summaryMs: when the log names every silent source and asks its getter once. A wrong factor is this one line, nothing else changes.

factors._verified: THE CAR, 2026-11-18: statusRangeTankStatus.mileageKilometre is km (factor 1, 114747 km); MileageSupreme.mileageSupreme carries METRES (114747213): factor 0.001 (shared/twin_tokens.js reads it as a UInt32).

odometer._about: research3/MK: the odometer (bottom row L1) from the first carrier with a valid value: rangeTank = KombiIF.statusRangeTankStatus.mileageKilometre, supreme = MileageSupreme.mileageSupreme (qualifier AVAILABLE / REDUCED only), range = VehicleInformation.Range.mileageKilometre, secure = SecureMileage.mileage.currentMileage. factors: km per bit (1 assumed). 0 and 16777215 or above = no value. verified: false = logged UNVERIFIED until compared with the cluster's own odometer.

dayNight._from: fix/colour-daynight, from the car's catalogue (reference/car/2026-11-15/someip/someip-interfaces.json): Vehicle (service 46352, instance 1) field statusDayNightChangeOver, getter 19, notifier 32787, struct StatusDayNightChangeOverWrapper { dayNightChangeOver: enum DayNightChangeOver (default 3), destinationLCDLuminance, dampingLCDLuminance }. DayNightChangeOver: 0 KEINE_AENDERUNG (no change: the last day/night the car gave holds; none yet: the sun), 1 TAG (day), 2 NACHT (night), 3 SIGNAL_UNGUELTIG (invalid: the sun). Any other value counts as invalid. The meaning of 0 is read off its German name only and is UNCONFIRMED on the car. 'codes' turns an enum NAME back into its number for the log (numbers only). hud.js _isNight.

clock._about: The car's own time-zone offset, so our clock is right without the manual timeZone setting (the owner, 2026-11-15; the head unit itself runs on UTC). Package X (2026-11-16): THIS IS THE FIRST SOURCE; the timeZone setting (if a build still has it) and config.utcOffsetMinutes are the fallbacks, in that order. A decoded offset is taken only if it is a whole number of quarter hours within +-14 h; anything else is logged once as 'clock: the car's offset decodes to N minutes ... ignored' and the next source is used. The line to check on the car: 'clock: ours shows HH:MM, UTC+hh:mm from ...' - it must read what the head unit's own clock reads.
clock._confirm: STILL AN UNCONFIRMED ENCODING, now LIVE. The catalogue says timeZonesOffsetAutomaticallyUTC is a UInt8 but not what one step is; "factor" 15 (quarter hours) is a guess. It was only parsed and logged while the manual "timeZone" setting existed; the owner retired that setting on 2026-11-15 ("забираємо все, можемо покластися на машину"), so the car's value is now the ONLY source our clock has and "confirm" is true. It could not be settled off the car: the 2026-11-15 snapshot has no captured value, and timeDateUTC's other members carry UTC, not local time, so there is nothing to difference against. THE FAILURE MODE IS A VISIBLY WRONG CLOCK, nothing worse, and one glance at the car settles it: compare our clock with BMW's own. If ours is out by a whole number of hours, the step is wrong - set "factor" to 1 (minutes), 30 (half hours) or 60 (hours) so the logged line 'clock: the car's offset would be N minutes' reads the real offset. If it is out by a constant that is not a multiple of the step, use "offsetBy" (subtracted from the raw first).
clock._log: fix/cclist (0.7.19): 0.7.18's 'clock raw:' line was cut at 100 characters, just before the three zone members, and repeated every 10 s (the seconds change). Now the WHOLE struct (all ten members of TimeDateUTCWrapper) is logged, uncut, once per change of the members named in logOn only. On the owner's car (2026-11-17) statusClockTimeDateUTC read UHRZEIT_UEBER_UTC_VERFUEGBAR_UND_UEBER_QUARZ_WEITERGEZAEHLT_OFFSETS_NICHT_VERFUEGBAR (the catalogue enum, value 3: 'UTC available, counted on by the quartz, OFFSETS NOT AVAILABLE') - the car itself says this struct carries no offset, so config.clockLocal below is what gives the zone there. The factor (15) is NOT changed: there is still no evidence for any step.

clockLocal._about: fix/cclist (0.7.19): the time zone's FALLBACK after config.clock (hud.js _tzSource): the local time the cluster shows, KombiIF statusShowTimeDate (ShowTimeDateWrapper displayHour / displayMinute; getter 30, notifier 32798), against the head unit's own UTC clock, rounded to 15 minutes (hud.js tzOf kind 'local'). An hour or minute out of range (the catalogue default 255) gives none. UNCONFIRMED on the car: that this field reaches the head unit, and that it carries LOCAL time (its sibling DisplayStatus.TimeDate is the same struct). The line to check: 'clock (local) raw: {...} -> 120' and 'clock: ours shows HH:MM, UTC+02:00 from the car's shown clock'. Set to null to drop it.

ccList._about: Several messages at once: the car cycles through this list, and ours steps through it on the same clock (the owner, 2026-11-15). Each element carries a short name and a colour; config.ccm.cycleMs is how long each one is shown. The stock order and timing are being measured in docs/G20-DESIGN-SPEC.md.
ccList._cclist: fix/cclist (0.7.19), the owner's car 2026-11-17: newCCMessage (config.ccm) sent NOTHING in 25 minutes, a door-open message included; ccList is live and carries the message on show. Resting: [id 0 GREEN symbol 6]; driver's door open: [id 15 WHITE symbol 2], name 16 characters; shut: id 0 again. So THIS is the primary source of 'a message shows' (an entry whose cCIdentifer is not in ignoreIds - from ONE test, hence configurable) and of our message's headline (cCShortName), colour and severity (cCColor) and symbol id (cCListSymbolID). newCCMessage stays wired as a second source; whichever says a message shows wins. The first notification that is a list whose entries fit 'root' ends the blind case (hud.js _ccWired). Member names from the catalogue: CCListElementUnion.cCListElement = CCListElementStruct { cCIdentifer (sic), cCShortName, cCListSymbolID, cCColor, cCIndentation, ricResourceID }. The text is never logged.

ccActive._about: fix/active-cc (0.7.20), the owner's car 2026-11-17: ccList lists the ACTIVE AND THE STORED messages - a ready-to-drive message (id 987) stayed listed after BMW hid it (~20 s), so 0.7.19 kept our message area open / drawn with nothing of BMW's on screen. This field, KombiIF statusActiveCCMessage, is taken as the cluster's own 'message shown now' (a HYPOTHESIS until the car confirms it). Every change is logged once, numbers only: 'active cc: number N control C frame F/G utility U'. Once it has notified with a number ('wired') it alone decides: a message shows iff numberPath is not in noneValues; text, colour and severity come from the ccList entry whose cCIdentifer equals that number. No such entry: still shown, BMW's panel stays open, our line empty, and 'active cc: no ccList entry for number N' is logged once per N - that line tells whether the two numberings match. The catalogue default of the number is 65535 (unfilled); it is NOT in noneValues, so it reads as shown with no entry: BMW's panel open (the safe side). shared/hud.js _ccListEval.
ccActive._fallback: A HEURISTIC, used only while statusActiveCCMessage has never given a number: a ccList entry counts as showing for hideAfterMs (null: config.ccm.autoHideMs, 20000 - BMW's manual's ~20 s auto-hide) after it was first listed; an entry whose colour is in keepColors shows for as long as it is listed. An entry that leaves the list and comes back starts its clock again. on: false gives back 0.7.19 (every listed entry shows while listed).
ccActive._strict: SPEC 8.4 / D7 (the owner, 2026-11-17): until statusActiveCCMessage has once delivered a number that matched a ccList entry, our plate is never drawn over BMW's panel: the fallback window opens whenever the heuristic says a message may show. Package D.
ccActive._release: twin_dial B3 (SPEC-R3 5.4.7, off): null, or { deferValues: [65535], leftList: "kept" } - the narrowed release: a shown-now value that is no verdict (65535, or a number whose ccList entry has left AFTER the number was set) lets the list decide. leftList true is research3/MC's wider rule and is unsafe (a returning door message whose number arrives before its list entry), never set it. shared/hud.js _ccRelease. car-fix CF1: it acts on the ACTIVE number only, so with source displayed it is obsolete (it can act only before displayed has spoken, and with dead true not even then).
ccActive._unlistedPullsTab: car-fix CF1 (the lead, 2026-11-18): a displayed number with NO ccList entry (285, 926, 927, 184 on the owner's car, ~6 s each, several per drive) keeps BMW's panel open but does not pull tab 2 and so shows no pointer page by itself - the driver reads BMW's own panel. Only a number that matches a ccList entry, or 65535 with a message in the list, pulls tab 2. true gives back the pull (SPEC-R3 5.1's pointer page). shared/twin_cc.js TwinCentre.
ccActive._carfix: car-fix CF1 (docs/car-fix/CF1-REPORT.md), the owner's car 2026-11-18 (signal_probe 0.1.1 and twin_dial.log): statusActiveCCMessage sat on 65535 the whole run, also while a message showed (dead: true - it stays declared, subscribed and logged, it decides nothing; without dead it would count as a witness only once it CHANGED to a number outside deadValues, default [65535]). Vehicle2.statusDisplayedCCMessage (config.ccDisplayed) is the real 'shown now' (source: displayed): door opened -> ccList id 15 and displayed 15 within ~50 ms; closed -> ccList at rest, displayed 0 0.2-0.7 s later; 14, 19 and 2255 matched their entries the same way; 285, 926, 927 and 184 showed with no ccList entry (BMW's panel stays open for them). unknownValues: 65535 on displayed (after an app start, at the end of a drive) is unknown: BMW's panel open, no tab pulled unless the list holds a message. confirmNow true: the numbering is car-verified (four ids), so D7 falls on the first match and THAT message's card may cover BMW's panel after its 150 ms (SPEC-R3 5.4.6 'until ... has once delivered'); false gives back 'ours from the next one'. shared/hud.js _ccListEval / _twinInputs, shared/twin_cc.js.

menu.comment: shared/menu.js: twin_dial has neither the drive-mode rows nor the G20 toggle

startupHold._about: B7 (research3/MP): the FIRST build waits until the car's first time zone and first message list are in, or ms after cluster-render is ready, whichever is first: one build at start instead of three (shared/diag_settings.js hold; the bytes before and after are in docs/twin-dial/R3B-INTEGRATION.md). Remove the key (or set false) for the three builds of 0.1.0.

diag._about: B7, the Діагностика menu (screen DIAG, shared/diag_settings.js): each setting writes the config paths named here while it is ON (every one is OFF by default = app.json's own key, put back when it goes off); a path is dotted; a choice lists its options. The changes apply in place (no layout rebuild).

diagRelease._about: the narrowed release of research3/MC for Twin Dial (SPEC-R3 5.4 step 7: only a number that was set before its entry left the list may be released; 65535 deferred): package B3 owns the engine side, this is the value the setting switches on

pages._about: round 3 B4 (SPEC-R3 4): the pages built DARK, each switched on by the car session once its signal has been seen (docs/AGENT-BRIEF-car-signals.md). tyres: tab 1's tyre page joins the cycle (TPMS getters polled every 10 s while it shows); media: tab 3's radio and now-playing pages (P8); phone: tab 4's call card (P9); guidance: tab 5's guidance page (P12). false = the certain page or the fallback shows.

config._mapWindow: round 3 B4 (SPEC-R3 4.5), an EXPERIMENT: null = no map window; "W1" = the soft-edged window (zero box [750, 180, 1170, 564], fades 120 / 80 / 80, corner 24), "W2" = open wider so that BMW's own edge shows. It opens only while tab 5 is selected and BMW's map is believed present (mapSlots / the cluster's map-view setting) and closes at once on any doubt. Needs B1's u_map uniform in tdback.
config._mapSlots: true once the experiment has shown that cluster-render's status rows (slot 0x100 ... map 1) are readable: the window then follows them (S1); false = it follows the cluster's map-view setting and guidance (S2).

sign._values: The raw speed values follow the convention of the car's own FASuS NextClassLimitSpeed enum, which is the only one in the catalogue that spells them out: 0 = AUFHEBUNG_ALLES (the end of all restrictions, the derestriction sign), 254 = NICHT_VERFUEGBAR and 255 = SIGNAL_UNBEFUELLT (no limit known, BMW's empty sign). displaySpeedLimit itself is a plain UInt8 with no names, so this is reasoning, not proof: the 'sign:' log line on the car settles it. "none" is empty on purpose - the owner's cluster essentially always shows a sign (2026-11-15).
sign._hold: The stock cluster animates the end of a limit and then shows the new one, and a sign is essentially always present (the owner, 2026-11-15), so there is no "hide the sign" state. holdMs keeps the last sign on while the car briefly says nothing; the animation itself lands in shared/hud.js _signShow().
sign._timings: changeFlashMs / flashPeriodMs are docs/G20-DESIGN-SPEC.md's PLACEHOLDERS for the flash after a limit changes - there is no video in the reference set, so nothing was measured. They are parameters only; nothing acts on them yet.
sign._empty: docs/G20-DESIGN-SPEC.md: BMW's empty sign is THREE DASHES, 8.8 x 4.4 at pitch 13, not a blank disc. That is WBSIGN's u_show state 3, which this package already drives; whether the shader draws dashes is the drawing package's to check.
sign._mph: The unit is read and recorded ({{limitUnit}}, the 'sign:' log line) but changes nothing on screen: the sign stays the round one with the number, in every country (the owner, 2026-11-15).

limit._about: SPEC-R3 8 (b): the speedometer's tick strip red from the limit. 'L1' = red from the limit's angle to the scale's end, dim while the needle is below the limit and full when over (SPEC-R3 8, the lead's reading); 'L2' = red only between the limit and the needle, only while over; 'L3' = as L1 but always full; 'off' = the marker only. The owner's choice (docs/twin-dial/MOCKUP-SPEC-R3B.md) is this one line. Not f30_cluster's config.limit (no iface / field here: nothing is subscribed by it).

config._cruise: SPEC-R3 9, built DARK: null = nothing is drawn and the layout does not even build the readout's sheet. { place: 'C1' | 'C2' } switches it on (C1 = the hub's lower part, C2 = the coolant bar's place); further keys (funcMap, statusMap, speedPath, factor, unitPath, mphOn, icons ...) correct what the car's values mean once the car session has shown the struct (shared/twin_limit.js CRUISE_DEFAULT).
